_note: Register: everyday standard Hausa, second person familiar (ka/ki mixed as context requires, defaulting masculine where a single form is needed, matching the pack's own convention) rather than the polite plural ku, since this is software chrome addressed to one user directly. Bare imperative verb stems on buttons (Fitarwa, Ajiye, Soke, Rufe) the way Hausa software UI conventionally does. Terms of art: a printed face is fuska and a sheet is takarda, so "faces/sheets" is fuska/takarda; duplex is bangarori biyu (two sides); typeface is nau'in rubutu; romanisation is rubutun Roman; the respelling field is Yadda ake fadinsa and the literal gloss Ainihin ma'ana; "glossed into" is An fassara zuwa. Romanisation systems keep their Latin/English names (ALA-LC, BGN/PCGN, ELOT 743, Hepburn, Hunterian, IAST, Kunrei-shiki, McCune-Reischauer, Okrand, Pinyin, RTGS) since Hausa has no settled calque for any of them, except roman.appendix-e and roman.rr, translated the way Indonesian's own catalogue translates the same two. Interpolation: Intl.DisplayNames hands Hausa a real language name already (Turanci, Larabci, Sinanci), not a bare ethnonym the way it hands Indonesian one, because the -anci/-nci suffix already means "language of" -- confirmed directly (Intl.DisplayNames(['ha']).of('ar') gives larabci, not just 'Larabawa') -- so no head-noun fix is needed on the {language} templates the way Indonesian's bahasa- prefix was.
